results_section_title: Spatial distribution and persistence of allocation gains and losses
results_paragraphs: At the 50% regional irrigation reduction, targeted allocation increased mean annual combined wheat–maize dry grain relative to uniform reduction on 43.92% of the mapped rotation area (4.333 Mha), decreased it on 37.60% (3.710 Mha), and left it unchanged on 18.48% (1.823 Mha). Mean contrasts within the gain and loss areas were +2.439 and -0.903 t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹, respectively. Their regional contributions were +10.568 and -3.349 Mt yr⁻¹, giving a net gain of 7.219 Mt yr⁻¹ (0.732 t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ across the full mapped area). Local losses offset 31.69% of the gross positive contribution.

The area-weighted median grain contrast was 0.000 t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹, and the 10th and 90th percentiles were -1.182 and +3.553 t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹. Thus, the positive regional mean coexisted with a substantial lower tail of local losses. Relative to uniform reduction, mean annual field irrigation increased by 119.0 mm in the gain area and decreased by 139.0 mm in the loss area. The corresponding modeled total evapotranspiration contrasts were +94.4 and -55.1 mm yr⁻¹. The irrigation transfers balanced at regional scale, whereas the evapotranspiration contrasts summed to a net increase of 20.8 mm yr⁻¹.

Local grain losses were persistent over 2014–2025: 21.34% of the mapped rotation area lost grain in all 12 years, and 37.60% experienced a loss in at least one year. Every response unit with a negative period-mean contrast recorded losses in at least 9 years; all response units with a positive period-mean contrast recorded gains in all 12 years. Across years, the mean annual area exposed to a loss was 35.37%. Loss cells formed 8 connected grid-cell footprints under rook adjacency. The largest contained 3.700 Mha of mapped rotation area (99.73% of all loss area), with occupied cell centers extending from 32.0 to 36.3°N and 112.8 to 121.5°E.

The distributional tradeoff increased as the regional irrigation budget tightened. Mean grain losses occupied 32.80%, 37.60%, and 60.08% of mapped rotation area at reductions of 25%, 50%, and 75%, respectively. At the 75% reduction, the area-weighted median contrast became negative (-0.788 t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), although gains on 37.04% of the area produced a positive regional balance. Gross positive and negative contributions at that reduction were +14.100 and -7.487 Mt yr⁻¹, leaving a net gain of 6.614 Mt yr⁻¹, below the net gain at the 50% reduction.
methods_paragraph: Spatial distribution statistics describe targeted-minus-uniform policy contrasts in mean annual combined wheat–maize dry grain and water fluxes over 2014–2025. The 3,641 mapped 0.1° source cells carry outcomes from 32 representative response units. Cell weights are the static 2020 mapped rotation areas after cropland-fraction correction; they represent mapped rotation area rather than observed harvested area. Gains and losses exceed +10⁻⁶ and fall below −10⁻⁶ kg ha⁻¹, respectively; contrasts within these bounds are classified as unchanged. Group means use rotation-area weights, regional contributions sum area multiplied by the corresponding contrast, and weighted quantiles use the inverse empirical cumulative area distribution. Annual loss frequencies use the same sign threshold across the 12 years. Connected loss footprints comprise occupied cells sharing a horizontal or vertical grid edge (rook adjacency). The statistics describe the conditional modeled allocation footprint; mapped cells do not provide independent replication or cell-specific validation.
